uphold.rule: §3333.1 constitutional; collateral source evidence admissible but jury has discretion (may, not must reduce); scope limited to professional negligence

interpretive.rule: §3333.1(b) premium evidence limited in practical utility; jury-discretion standard established; practical framework for §3333.1 trial presentation

sirva_collateral_source_plan: Identify total amount Blue Shield (or other insurer) paid for shoulder surgery-related treatment
Compile Michael's premium payments history (monthly premiums + any co-pays/deductibles)
Determine if subrogation demand has been received from Blue Shield — if so, note under §3333.1(c) that subrogation right is eliminated if defense introduces insurance evidence

Assess whether SIRVA claim can be framed as negligent injection technique (professional negligence = §3333.1 applies) or willful misconduct (intentional = §3333.1 may not apply; see SIRVA doctrine standard for PREP Act analysis)
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.spine_surgery_hrimnak_escape: If spine surgery claim is framed as fraud/battery/lack of informed consent (Hrimnak doctrine), §3333.1 does not apply. All insurance payments are excluded from collateral source evidence. Full economic damages for surgery costs, rehabilitation, ongoing treatment, and lost earnings available without §3333.1 reduction.
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.anti_subrogation_coordination: Before trial, notify Blue Shield and any other insurer that defense has introduced (or will introduce) §3333.1 evidence. Under §3333.1(c), once introduced, the insurer has no subrogation right against Michael's recovery. Get this in writing before settlement to ensure insurer waives its lien.
